about: Curated by the monitor, NOT by the research team. Each repo_results entry cites a verbatim quote and Lean theorem names; the server re-checks every quote and theorem against the live files on each refresh and flags any that no longer match. The live findings/STATE/commits shown elsewhere are authoritative; this file only frames complexity and units so toy counts are never promoted to end-to-end speedups.

problem.name: secp256k1 ECDLP (full-size key recovery)
problem.statement: Given public Q = [d]G on secp256k1 with prime group order n, recover d in [0, n).
problem.not_key_generation: Key generation (choose d, compute Q=[d]G) is cheap: one scalar multiplication. All workloads here are for the inverse problem, key recovery.

classical_references.formula: up to n group operations (worst case)
about 2*sqrt(n) group operations worst case with m = ceil(sqrt(n)) stored points
classical_references.memory: about sqrt(n) = 2^128 stored points: the memory alone is physically infeasible

source.label: Handbook of Applied Cryptography ch. 3, alg. 3.56

classical_references.formula: known constant-factor saving (order sqrt(2)) on additions; same sqrt(n) exponent
classical_references.status: published constant-factor technique; repo has finite experiments only (W006/W012)

classical_references.formula: on average approximately 0.886*sqrt(l) additions (SafeCurves; lists 2^127.8 for secp256k1)
classical_references.status: best known generic attack; expected-case, randomized

classical_references.formula: Omega(sqrt(q)) group operations for any generic algorithm
classical_references.status: theorem (Shoup 1997) for generic algorithms only; a break must exploit the representation

source.label: Shoup, Lower bounds for discrete logarithms

rounded_reference_note: The repo's own illustrative workload (Research/Goals.lean uses 2^128). SafeCurves' finer rho figure is 2^127.8 additions.

rate_source.label: RCKangaroo README: 19.3 GH/s on RTX 5090 (turbo kernels)
rate_source.units: Reported kangaroo-method curve-walk steps per second on a bounded-range search. The README does not define one 'operation' precisely; treat as roughly one point addition-like step. Not a measurement of full-size rho.

assumptions: ILLUSTRATIVE EXTRAPOLATION, not a measured full-size attack.
Workload is key RECOVERY (inverse problem); ordinary key generation is a single cheap scalar multiplication.
Perfect linear scaling across GPUs, 100% utilization, no distinguished-point, memory, communication or failure overhead.
Expected (average) work for a randomized method, not a worst-case guarantee.
1 year = 365.25 days. GPU-years = years x GPUs (independent of GPU count under perfect scaling).
No repo algorithm has a validated mapping to these units; the repo's cost units (equality tests, query comparisons, word-actions) must not be plugged in here.
